mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals an easing monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days regardless of market conditions.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where FEDFUNDS has declined over the prior 3 months, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.0% signals labor market deterioration that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 4.0% over 3 months, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate broad consumer demand contraction that lowers corporate revenue expectations, driving negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where both HOUST and RSAFS decline over 3 months, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: High industrial production growth (INDPRO > 110.0) indicates eased supply constraints that lower input costs and boost corporate margins, generating positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where INDPRO exceeds 110.0, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Accelerating inflation (CPIAUCSL yoy > 2.5%) triggers anticipated Federal Reserve tightening that increases equity discount rates, causing negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where CPIAUCSL yoy exceeds 2.5%, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained strong labor market growth (PAYEMS > 200.0) indicates rising consumer spending power that supports corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where PAYEMS exceeds 200.0, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Housing market contraction (HOUST < 1100.0) signals reduced consumer spending capacity that depresses corporate revenue growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where HOUST falls below 1100.0, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in industrial production (INDPRO) and rises in unemployment (UNRATE) indicate economic slowdown with supply and labor market deterioration, driving negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where INDPRO declines and UNRATE rises, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
